That is Hook.cs:928-954's Early/plain/Late three-pass structure, and it puts the Earring after the plain-pass implementers it must follow — enchantments.py:315 (Imbued, the very case WhisperingEarring.cs's doc comment at :38-40 names) and powers.py:3768 both sit in the plain pass. So step-22/23 listeners (Vexing Puzzlebox, Crossbow, …) are all finished before the Earring's loop opens, whatever order run.relics is in.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: MECHANISM: Hook.AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered runs AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEnteredEarly, then AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEntered, then AfterAutoPrePlayPhaseEnteredLate as three separate complete passes (Hook.cs:928-955) -- PROMPT.md bug class 25 -- and CombatManager.RunAutoPrePlayPhase enters the phase strictly after Hook.AfterSideTurnStart and the orb queue (CombatManager.cs:556-572). The sim has neither the phase nor the pass structure (audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 26 and guard G8), so whispering_earring.py:27 fires from on_player_turn_started alongside every step-22 and step-23 listener in a single `for l in list(self._listeners)` loop (hooks.py:285-295). guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the port routes an AUTO-play through the MANUAL play path, so nothing downstream can tell these plays were automatic
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 6): the loop auto-plays. WhisperingEarring.cs:78-80 is `await card.SpendResources(); await CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, card, target, AutoPlayType.Default, skipXCapture: true)` -- the energy is paid by SpendResources (CardModel.cs:1816-1829) and the play itself is an AUTO-play, so the resulting CardPlay carries IsAutoPlay. relics/whispering_earring.py used `combat.play_card`, the manual path, so every `is_auto_play` listener -- Tuning Fork's counter among them -- counted these as real plays. It now spends the modified energy cost explicitly (including the X-cost capture) and calls `combat.auto_play_card`, which is the free path. The cost gate is unchanged, so the loop still stops when nothing is affordable. Pinned by test_whispering_earring_plays_are_auto_plays.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: WhisperingEarring.cs:79-80 does `await card.SpendResources()` and then `CardCmd.AutoPlay(choiceContext, card, target, AutoPlayType.Default, skipXCapture: true)`, which ends in `card.OnPlayWrapper(..., isAutoPlay: true, ...)` (CardCmd.cs:51-128) -- so the resulting CardPlay carries IsAutoPlay. whispering_earring.py:43 calls `combat.play_card(playable[0] - 1)`, the manual path (combat.py:381-421), even though the sim HAS an auto-play surface the Imbued enchantment already uses (CombatState.auto_play, combat.py:423-438, and auto_play_card, combat.py:516-546, which passes `auto_play=True` to should_play_card). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py earring-auto): with relics=[whispering_earring, brilliant_scarf], Brilliant Scarf's counter reads 5 after the Earring's turn-1 loop, where C# leaves it at 0 because BrilliantScarf.AfterCardPlayed returns early on `cardPlay.IsAutoPlay` (BrilliantScarf.cs:84-87). Both relics are ported Ancients and co-obtainable. Every card the Earring plays therefore shifts which card Brilliant Scarf makes free, for the rest of that turn. RULE 3 boundary, stated explicitly: audit/records/relic/brilliant_scarf.json guard G1 verdicts 'the sim's on_card_played carries no auto-play flag' a LIVE gap, and this entry does NOT re-derive that; what this entry adds is a divergence in THIS relic's own port -- it manufactures manual plays where the game manufactures auto-plays, so even a fixed Brilliant Scarf would still count them. TWO SUB-CLAUSES CHECKED AND FOUND FAITHFUL, so they are not part of the gap: (i) the card SELECTION agrees, because C#'s `CanPlay()` asks Hook.ShouldPlay with AutoPlayType.None (CardModel.cs:1755) -- the manual arm -- so Enthralled (Enthralled.cs:21-38, ported at sts2_rl/cards/enthralled.py:41-46, the only ported ShouldPlay implementer that distinguishes the two) blocks the same cards on both sides, executed in the same probe; (ii) energy accounting agrees, because C#'s SpendResources -> SpendEnergy fires Hook.AfterEnergySpent with the real cost (CardModel.cs:1816-1843) and the sim's play_card fires on_energy_spent with the real cost (combat.py:411-412), so the ported listener sts2_rl/relics/intimidating_helmet.py:19-22 behaves identically. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardModel.cs, combat.py, BrilliantScarf.cs, Enthralled.cs, sts2_rl/cards/enthralled.py, sts2_rl/relics/intimidating_helmet.py and audit/records/relic/brilliant_scarf.json are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): C# pushes VakuuCardSelector for the whole loop, making every selection screen deterministic; the sim installs nothing and selects at random
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The loop pushes a deterministic selector. WhisperingEarring.cs:54 wraps the whole auto-play loop in `using (CardSelectCmd.PushSelector(new VakuuCardSelector()))`, and VakuuCardSelector.GetSelectedCards is `options.Take(maxSelect).ToList()` in row-major order (VakuuCardSelector.cs:16-19) -- fully deterministic, with NO RNG draw. relics/whispering_earring.py now installs `lambda purpose, candidates, count: list(candidates)[:count]` as `combat.card_selector` for the duration of the loop and restores the previous selector in a `finally`, which is the `using` block's semantics (and stops a real agent's selector being lost). The loop body moved into `_auto_play_loop` unchanged. WAS: no selector at all, so `CombatState.select_cards` fell through to `self._rng.sample(candidates, count)` -- the Earring auto-playing Armaments upgraded twin_strike on seeds 0 and 3 and bash on 1, 2 and 4, where C# always upgrades the FIRST option. Two observables, both closed: the wrong card was picked, AND the sim consumed shared-rng draws the game does not consume at all. EXECUTED: the Earring's turn-1 loop over a pinned hand now produces the SAME upgrade across five seeds (it produced three different outcomes), and the installed selector returns `candidates[:count]` for count 1 and 2. The pairing needs no second relic -- eight ported cards open a selection screen from OnPlay. Pinned by test/test_relic_live_tail.py's two whispering_earring tests. NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: WhisperingEarring.cs:54 wraps the loop in `using (CardSelectCmd.PushSelector(new VakuuCardSelector()))`, and VakuuCardSelector.GetSelectedCards is `options.Take(maxSelect)` in row-major order (VakuuCardSelector.cs:17-20) -- fully deterministic, with no RNG draw. The port installs no selector, and CombatState.select_cards falls back to `self._rng.sample(candidates, count)` when `card_selector` is None (combat.py:560-581). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b17.py earring-auto): the Earring auto-playing Armaments (a ported Ironclad Common whose OnPlay opens an upgrade selection, sts2_rl/cards/armaments.py:41) upgrades twin_strike on seeds 0 and 3 and bash on seeds 1, 2 and 4, with `card_selector = None` in every case; C# always upgrades the FIRST option. Both sides ported and the pairing needs no second relic: Armaments reaches the opening hand from the starting deck or any card reward, and eight ported cards open selection screens from OnPlay (grep `select_cards|CardSelectCmd` over sts2_rl/cards/ -- armaments, brand, burning_pact, headbutt, colorless_attacks, colorless_skills x4). Two distinct observables, not one: the wrong card is picked, AND the sim consumes shared-RNG draws the game does not consume at all. Rule 7: VakuuCardSelector.cs, combat.py, sts2_rl/cards/armaments.py and the other card modules named are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: `CombatManager.Instance.IsPlayerReadyToEndTurn(player)` is one of the loop's three break conditions (WhisperingEarring.cs:64-67) and has no sim counterpart
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 5): `IsPlayerReadyToEndTurn(player)` is ported. `CombatState.is_player_ready_to_end_turn` reads the deferred end-turn transition, which is the same instant with one player (`AllPlayersReadyToEndTurn`, CombatManager.cs:695), and the relic's loop breaks on all three of WhisperingEarring.cs:58-69's conditions in the source's order -- IsOverOrEnding, IsPlayerReadyToEndTurn, then the turn change. The middle one was unreachable until turn_structure N1 gave the sim somewhere to record a deferred end-turn.  The text it replaced read: The sim's loop breaks on `combat.is_over` and `self.turn != start_turn` (whispering_earring.py:38) but has no notion of a player having signalled 'end turn'. In the game this matters because the AutoPrePlay phase is asynchronous and the local player may already have pressed End Turn. DORMANT: the sim's driver is synchronous -- on_player_turn_started runs to completion inside PlayerCombatState.start_turn (player.py:185) before any agent action is possible, so no ready-to-end-turn state can exist while the loop runs, and there is no `ready_to_end_turn` concept anywhere in sts2_rl (grep returns nothing). Filed as a gap rather than a waiver because 'the sim has no such system' is a dormant gap under binding rule 1, not out of scope; what would make it live is any asynchronous or interruptible turn model. Rule 7: player.py is NOT hashed here.

guards.what: N2: the card the loop picks -- C#'s `pile.Cards.FirstOrDefault(c => c.CanPlay())` (WhisperingEarring.cs:72-73) vs the sim's first entry of valid_actions (whispering_earring.py:40-43)
guards.rationale: combat.valid_actions (combat.py:687-704) walks the hand in index order and admits a card when `card.is_playable`, `hooks.should_play_card(card)` and the hook-modified cost is affordable; `playable[0] - 1` is therefore the lowest playable hand index, matching FirstOrDefault over the hand pile. CanPlay's clause list (CardModel.cs:1734-1763) is the same set plus two the sim cannot reach: the Unplayable KEYWORD (the sim folds unplayability into `is_playable`) and `TargetType.AnyAlly && living player creatures <= 1`, which is multiplayer-only. Both break when nothing is playable. EXECUTED in the earring-auto probe via the Enthralled case, where both sides pick Enthralled itself first.

guards.what: N3: MAX_CARDS = 13 (whispering_earring.py:22) vs `public const int maxCardsToPlay = 13` and the literal `cardsPlayed < 13` (WhisperingEarring.cs:21, 58)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file; 13 is unconditional and appears as a bare literal in the loop bound as well as in the named const. `for _ in range(self.MAX_CARDS)` gives the same 13 iterations, and each sim iteration corresponds to one C# `cardsPlayed++` even when the play is refused, because both count attempts rather than successes.
